title: The Lovers

seo.title: Destiny matrix 6 — The Lovers: meaning of the arcanum
seo.description: 6 in the destiny matrix is the arcanum of The Lovers: attraction, union and choice. What the six means as a number, its strong and weak sides.

meaning: Six in the destiny matrix is the arcanum of The Lovers, the energy of attraction and union. The simplest way to describe it is with one sign: the six is the “and” between people, the point where two of them find each other. This person’s strength switches on not alone but in a pair — one plus one gives them not two, but noticeably more.

To be a six means living on response. The main driver here is neither will nor an idea but resonance: the energy lights up when someone answers — a glance, a liking, a “yes” coming back. Hence the steady inner hum of “is this my person, is this my place”, which sounds quietly even in calm years. Such a person measures life less by what they have done than by whom they did it with and who stood beside them.

Sewn into this energy is one eternal question — choice, because a union always comes down to “with whom exactly”. This is where the arcanum’s main test lies. The strong version is the one who can make up their mind and then stand by it: they become a bridge, they join people who do not work together apart, and they hold that tie for years. The weak version gets stuck in an endless “maybe”: it stays open to everyone at once, just to be liked, and so it truly belongs to no one.

It is easy to mistake the six for plain sociability. The point is not that the person likes people, but that their fate runs through someone else: growth, turning points, the very feeling of “I am in my place” are born not inside but at the joint with another. That is why both the joy and the main mistakes of this arcanum always have somebody’s face; they do not appear in silence, alone with oneself.

Neighbouring arcana help you feel the six by contrast. The seventh, The Chariot, goes out into the world on its own — by its own will, towards its own victory, asking nobody. The same road taken solo is hard for the six: without a companion the movement loses its sense, because its strength is not in arriving first but in arriving together.

article.title: Arcanum 6 in the destiny matrix: The Lovers — love that chooses
article.short: In the destiny matrix, 6 is The Lovers, the energy of love, attraction and choice. Its main idea is a single one: to love is to choose. A person with a strong 6 is easy to like, has a fine feel for people and for beauty, and can bring together those who could not come to terms on their own. Their lesson is to do the choosing themselves: not to keep two options open, not to wait for someone else’s approval and not to trade a living person for a perfect picture. It is the most widespread arcanum in the matrix: 85% of people have a 6 in at least one position of their reading.

seo.title: Destiny matrix 6: The Lovers — meaning, program and karmic tail
seo.description: Destiny matrix 6 is The Lovers: to love is to choose. Why its minus turns cynical, where a 6 sits in your date, program 6, eight tails and couples.

sections.h2: What 6 means in the destiny matrix
paragraphs: In the destiny matrix the 6 is described with two words, love and choice, and they are often presented as two separate meanings. In fact they are one. You can fall for several people at once, for a voice, for an image, for a lucky coincidence — falling in love simply happens. Love begins later: at the moment when, out of many, you choose one — a person, a cause, a city — and go on choosing it when others turn up nearby. The energy of 6 is the passage from “I’m drawn to” to “I choose”, and on to “we’re together”.

So the arcanum has three layers. **Attraction** — a pull towards people and towards beauty: a phrase put just right, a happy combination of colours, a person who lights up when talking about the thing they love. **Choice** — a decision made with the heart, from your own values, not from a table of pros and cons. **Union** — the ability to connect: yourself with another, people with each other, sides that until then spoke different languages.

A strong 6 is quick to spot. Half an hour into a room full of strangers, this person knows who has fallen out with whom and is already sitting between them. They spend three weeks choosing a present, because a present has to be “about that person”. Their home has no random objects — or, on the contrary, is full of them, because choosing just one never quite happened. What matters to them is not only what is said but how. People like them, and they know it.

The 6 has one theme without which nothing else works: choosing yourself. Whoever finds it hard to choose themselves chooses the people who will approve of them, and calls it love. That is why the arcanum’s lesson is often put as self-love — meaning not vanity but the right to your own “I want” and “I don’t want” beside the people you love.

sections.h2: The 6 in the plus and in the minus: why the arcanum of love can turn cynical

paragraphs: Lists of the 6’s minuses usually include words that sit badly with love: pessimism, cynicism, jealousy, fault-finding. They stop being surprising once you notice that almost every minus is a way of not choosing. There are three such ways.

**Not choosing.** Keeping both options open: two people, two jobs, two cities. It feels as if you lose nothing that way. In fact the options get tired of waiting, and the decision is made by someone else — a partner, a boss, circumstances. A postponed choice is a choice too, only not yours.

**Handing the choice to others.** Deciding the way parents, friends, colleagues or “normal people” would approve. The choice comes out right but belongs to someone else, and life inside it feels borrowed. Hence the resentment towards those who “made me”, although nobody made anyone do anything: they were simply handed the right to decide.

**Choosing an ideal instead of a person.** Falling in love with a picture and then measuring a living person against it. The picture never makes mistakes, never gets tired and is never in a bad mood — the living person loses to it every day. First comes criticism, then jealousy and control (“I’ll just check, in case he’s not who I think he is”), then the conclusion “they’re all the same”. A cynic with a 6 is a disappointed romantic: they loved the ideal for too long and decided not to love at all any more.
The plus of the 6 starts with the opposite move: make the choice, say so out loud, and stand by it when other options turn up.

sections.h2: Where the 6 sits in the matrix: check your date
paragraphs: In the destiny matrix, sums greater than 22 are reduced by adding up their digits. So a 6 comes not only from 6 but from 24, 33, 42 and even 51. Numbers up to 22 are not reduced, and this is where the most common mistake happens: **15 does not turn into 6**. Someone born on the 15th gets the fifteenth arcanum, The Devil, in their personality portrait, not The Lovers, as it would be in ordinary numerology. The same goes for years: 1950 gives 1 + 9 + 5 + 0 = 15, and that is The Devil again.

head: Point
When it is a 6
Share of people
rows: the sum A + B + C gives 6, 24, 33, 42 or 51
the sum A + B + C + D reduces to 6
calculated from the sums of the purposes

paragraphs: Example: 24 June 1986. Day 24 → 2 + 4 = 6, month 6, year 1 + 9 + 8 + 6 = 24 → 6. Three sixes in the outer points, and the karmic task is 6 + 6 + 6 = 18, The Moon.

85.0% of people have a 6 in at least one position of their reading — more than for any other arcanum: for the rest the figure ranges from 13.4 to 84.3%. That is arithmetic, not a mark of the chosen: several common sums reduce to 6 at once.

The 6 is even more noticeable in the spiritual purpose — one person in five has it there. This point has only seven possible values in the first place: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 and 21. That is how the sum it comes from is built. The same holds for point M, the entry of relationships and the tail. And in both points the 6 has a single cellmate: 15. If A + B + C leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by 3, the spiritual purpose can only be 6 or 15; if the remainder is 2, the same thing happens at point M. The attraction that chooses and the attraction that binds share one seat in the chart.

The outer points also set the decades of life. For those born on the 6th and the 24th, childhood up to the age of 10 passes under The Lovers; for those born in June, the years from 20 to 30; for those born in the years from the table, the years from 40 to 50. 46.5% of people have at least one decade under the 6.

Several sixes in one chart do not mean “double love”. The record is ten points: for example, people born on 18 June 1971 have a 6 in the spiritual and karmic tasks and in all four family lines. Each of these sixes is read in its own role: one and the same theme of choice sounds now as an inner question, now as a family story, now as a money channel.

paragraphs: A year can also pass under the 6. It is a year of people and of choosing between them: options turn up on their own, and the year demands that you decide with whom and in what to invest. In detail: [on the year page](/year/6).

Next to other arcana the 6 changes its shade. With The Hanged Man (12) love gets stuck in waiting; with The Devil (15) attraction pulls hard and not always in the right direction; with The Hermit (9) the person reaches out to people and at once withdraws into themselves; with Strength (11) attraction turns into reliability. These and other pairs are covered on the combination pages: [6 and 12](/encyclopedia/combination/6-12), [6 and 15](/encyclopedia/combination/6-15), [6 and 9](/encyclopedia/combination/6-9), [6 and 11](/encyclopedia/combination/6-11).

A search for “program 6” means that a 6 stands in a point where the matrix reads repeating scripts. In our reading this is the section “Programs: what repeats in circles”, made of three lines: the karmic task D is the root of the storyline, the centre E is the state in which the autopilot switches on, and the spiritual purpose is the way out. 40.7% of people have a 6 in at least one of them. How programs work in general is covered on the [page about programs](/programs) and in the [report section](/encyclopedia/position/loops); here the subject is how the 6 in particular goes round.

Its loop is recognised by the ending: someone else makes the decision. A second option appears — a person, a job, a city. To choose means to disappoint someone, so the person stalls: tells both “almost yes”, waits for a sign, asks everyone’s advice. The options get tired of waiting. One leaves of its own accord, the other issues an ultimatum, or circumstances decide for everyone. What remains is the feeling “it’s always like this with me” — and next time the person is even more careful about choosing, which means they stall even longer. The storyline can be entirely mundane, too: spending six months choosing between two flats until both are let to someone else, or weighing two job offers for so long that both are withdrawn.
The role of the 6 depends on the line.

ul: **6 at the root (D).** A fork in the road sets the storyline going. Until the choice is made, life keeps handing it back: different people, the same question.

**6 in the centre (E).** Under pressure the autopilot is to adapt: to guess what the other person expects and become convenient. An early warning is the phrase “let’s do it your way”, said when you want something else.

**6 at the exit point (spiritual purpose).** This is the case for one person in five. Whatever the program is about — money, control, grievances — what helps to break the circle is a decision of the heart, spoken out loud, with a readiness to lose the other option.

paragraphs: You can test the program of the 6 against your own story. Recall two occasions when a decision was made for you, and ask yourself what you were doing the week before it was settled. If both times you were waiting, stalling and saying “no” to nobody, that is the one.

The karmic tail is the set of three numbers in the lower part of the chart, read in the order M–N–D: entry, middle, root. 20.9% of people have a 6 in the tail, and it can take any of the three places:

ul: **at the entry (M)** the script starts with attraction — the wish to be liked, to be chosen, to fall in love;
**in the middle (N)** the loop is held together by a union — by a bond that is hard to let go of;
**at the root (D)** stands the task of the tail: to choose for yourself and to love a living person, not an image.

paragraphs: For dates since 1900 there are eight tails with a 6. In five of them it stands at the entry. When the 6 is in the middle, the entry is always The Moon (18): attraction seen by reflected light. Each tail has its own page:

paragraphs: The most common of them, 18-6-6, is the seventh most widespread of all 26 tails in the matrix. A general guide to reading a tail is in the [section on the karmic tail](/encyclopedia/position/past_lives).

Compatibility in the destiny matrix is not worked out by comparing two numbers. Tables like “6 goes well with 2, 4 and 14” compare arcana, not people. A couple’s matrix is built differently: the matching points of two personal matrices are added together and the sum is reduced to 1–22. A 6 appears in the couple’s matrix when the sum gives 6, 24, 33 or 42. For example, if one partner’s centre is 8 and the other’s is 16, the couple’s centre will be 8 + 16 = 24 → 6.

According to Yuliana Lisovskaya’s book Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility), the 6 in a couple is love as a daily choice: tenderness, openness, deciding together even on small things, generosity and a beautiful life. In the minus — a seesaw of “peace one day, war the next”, jealousy born of insecurity and words that wound. Almost one couple in three has the 6 in their common language; what it means there and at the couple’s other points is on a separate page about the 6 in compatibility. The method gives no compatibility percentages.

sections.h2: The 6 for women and for men
paragraphs: The calculation is the same for a man and a woman: gender plays no part in the method, and people born on the same date have the same numbers. What differs is not the arcanum but the script the surroundings offer around it. This is about other people’s expectations, not about what a person is obliged to be.

A woman with a strong 6 is readily handed the role of the one who charms, reconciles and adorns. The trap is that “being liked” easily stands in for “choosing”: she becomes the one who gets chosen and fails to notice that she herself has not chosen anything for a long time. Her choices are also more often discussed by others — “she’s too picky”, “it’s time she made up her mind” — and a 6 in the minus hands the decision over to this chorus.

A man with a strong 6 more often has to defend what he has: taste, attention to people, a willingness to talk seriously about relationships. The trap is hiding it behind “I don’t mind, you choose”. It sounds accommodating, but in fact the choice has simply been shifted onto someone else — and the responsibility with it.

sections.h2: Waite’s Lovers: the picture on the card and where “choice” came from
paragraphs: On Waite’s card, drawn by Pamela Colman Smith in 1909, the sun stands at its zenith. Beneath it is a great winged figure with arms outstretched, which, in the author’s words, is “pouring down influences”. The angel is usually called Raphael, although Waite himself gives no name. Below are a naked man and woman, “as if Adam and Eve when they first occupied the paradise of the earthly body”. Behind the man stands the Tree of Life; behind the woman, the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil, with the serpent twining round it. Between them, in the distance, a mountain rises.

Two details are worth a closer look. The Tree of Life in Waite’s description bears twelve fruits, like the tree of life in the Book of Revelation; in the drawing they look like tongues of flame. And the gazes: the man looks at the woman, and the woman looks up at the angel. In the twentieth century Paul Foster Case read this as a ladder: self-consciousness turns to subconsciousness, and subconsciousness to superconsciousness. Benebell Wen in “Holistic Tarot” sees in the man “the mind and rationality”, in the woman “the heart and emotion”, and in the card itself a choice “between the mind and the heart”.

Waite himself put the meaning briefly: “This is in all simplicity the card of human love” — of “youth, virginity, innocence and love before it is contaminated by gross material desire”, shown “as part of the way, the truth and the life”. “In a very high sense,” he adds, “the card is a mystery of the Covenant and Sabbath.” About the woman he writes separately: she is “rather the working of a Secret Law of Providence than a willing and conscious temptress”.

Choice came to this card from the old decks, and Waite argued with it. In fifteenth-century Italian decks the card was called Love (L’Amore): on the Milanese Visconti–Sforza cards a couple join hands as at a betrothal, and a blindfolded Cupid hovers above them. In the Tarot de Marseille it became L’Amoureux, “The Lover”, in the singular: a young man stands between two women, and Cupid takes aim downwards from a circle of sun. The women were read in different ways — as Vice and Virtue, after the story of Hercules at the crossroads, or as a mother and a bride. Waite saw in the old card a scene of married life, “shewing father and mother, with their child placed between them”, and called the later pictures “follies which depicted man between vice and virtue”. His own card, he says, replaces them “by recourse to first principles”: instead of a choice, Adam and Eve. The destiny matrix inherited both lines, Waite’s love and the Marseille tradition’s choice — hence the two words the 6 is known by.

For divination Waite gives the arcanum a short list. Upright: “Attraction, love, beauty, trials overcome.” Reversed: “Failure, foolish designs. Another account speaks of marriage frustrated and contrarieties of all kinds.” In the destiny matrix there are no reversed cards: a number taken from a date of birth lies neither upright nor upside down. Instead of the card’s position, the plus and the minus of the energy are read.

In the Golden Dawn system, to which Waite belonged, The Lovers is linked with the sign of Gemini. A coincidence, but an amusing one: Gemini covers the end of May and most of June, and in the destiny matrix people born in June get a 6 in the spiritual task.

And one more rhyme in Waite’s deck. The fifteenth arcanum, The Devil, repeats the composition of The Lovers: again a winged figure above, again a man and a woman below — but now with little horns and tails, chained to a pedestal. The chains round their necks are loose; they could be lifted off. It is the same scene of attraction, only here the choice has been given away. In the matrix these arcana are neighbours too: the points where either a 6 or a 15 falls are covered above, and their meeting in one chart is discussed in [the combination of 6 and 15](/encyclopedia/combination/6-15).

sections.h2: How to live the 6 in the plus
paragraphs: Working with the 6 always comes down to one skill: making a choice and holding to it. Here are five exercises, each with a time frame and a first step.

ol: **A decision with a date.** Take a choice that has been hanging for more than a month. Write down the options, set a decision day no more than two weeks away, and before that day tell the person it concerns. You may postpone again only out loud and with a new date.

**The secret ballot.** Before an important decision, answer on paper: what would I choose if no one ever found out about my choice? The gap between this answer and what you are about to do is the share of other people’s votes in the decision.

**A living person instead of a portrait.** Once a week, notice one thing someone close to you did differently from the picture you hold of them — and that you treasure in them. An ideal cannot do that; only a living person can.
**One “no” a week.** A 6’s “yes” is worth something only if it can also say “no”. Once a week, refuse where you would otherwise agree just so as not to disappoint.

**Choice in small things.** Every day, choose one thing purely on the principle “I like it”: a mug, the way home, the music in the car — without asking anyone’s opinion. The ability to choose is trained where a mistake costs nothing.

sections.h2: What this reading is based on

ul: The picture, symbolism and divinatory meanings of the card follow A. E. Waite’s “The Pictorial Key to the Tarot” (1922 reissue), illustrated by Pamela Colman Smith.
The reading of the card as a choice, and how it differs from The Devil, follow Benebell Wen’s “Holistic Tarot” (2015).
The 6 in a couple’s matrix follows Yuliana Lisovskaya’s “Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost” (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024).
The points are calculated by Natalia Ladini’s scheme. The shares of people were counted by the site’s engine over every date from 1 January 1900 to 5 October 2026.
The history of the card draws on the Visconti–Sforza decks (fifteenth century) and the Tarot de Marseille.

paragraphs: The destiny matrix is a system of interpretation, not a science: it describes tendencies and repeating scripts, but it does not predict events.
